# bluestonepim_relation (Resource)

A product relation type, for example a "Superseded by" relation between an old and a new product.

A relation that is used by product connections is only deleted with `force_destroy = true`, which also removes all those product connections.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "bluestonepim_relation" "successor" {
  name         = "Superseded by"
  reverse_name = "Successor of"
  number       = "successor"
  description  = "The product that replaces this one."
  direction    = "TWO_WAY"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The name of the relation.

### Optional

- `description` (String) The description of the relation.
- `direction` (String) `ONE_WAY`: the relation is visible on the product it is added to. `TWO_WAY`: it is visible on the products on both sides. Changing `ONE_WAY` to `TWO_WAY` is only possible when the relation has no product connections. Set by Bluestone when not set.
- `force_destroy` (Boolean) Delete the relation even when it is used by product connections, which removes all those connections. Without it, deleting a relation that is in use fails.
- `number` (String) The number of the relation, to identify it in imports and integrations. Generated by Bluestone when not set.
- `quantity_enabled` (Boolean) Whether a quantity can be set on the product connections of this relation.
- `reverse_name` (String) The name of the relation as seen from the other product, for example "Successor of". Shown for `TWO_WAY` relations.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Platform-generated unique identifier of the relation.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import bluestonepim_relation.successor <relation_id>
```
